# Migration Checklist: A resource is a database

**Purpose**: Review the requirements that remove the data source, move a domain onto the entity and put the check on return, so that no old name, rule or page is left behind when the change ships.
**Created**: 2026-11-07
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: Custom checklist generated by `/speckit-checklist` for this feature.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Removal completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is every removed public name enumerated — `BaseDataSource`, `InMemoryDataSource`, `ExternalServiceDataSource`, the data source graph node and its edges, the resource generic parameter — rather than summarised as "data sources"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the removal of `resource=` from `@entity` stated as a refusal, with the error the reader sees, not only as an omission? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK003 Does each removed rule of #475 and #479 have its own requirement, naming the refusal it used to cause? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the places a removed name may hide — exports, package facades, tests, examples, notebooks, pages, the saved graph — all named? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005, §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK005 Is it stated whether the old names may remain anywhere, and where exactly (specs, historical changelogs, labelled migration fragments)? [Clarity, Spec §SC-001]

## Declaration migration

- [ ] CHK006 Is "an entity names its domain" defined precisely enough to say what an entity with no domain does? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK007 Does the spec say what `@meta` refuses on a resource, and what it still requires on an action, so the two rules cannot contradict? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK008 Is `@entities` defined for the empty list and for a listed class that is not an `@entity`, with the refusal each produces? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-003, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK009 Is it stated that a relation may cross databases and that an action glues their data, rather than left to the reader's inference from the removed rules? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK010 Are the kinds that may declare `@entities` and the reason (what the declaration promises) recorded, so a later reader does not reintroduce a storage-only rule? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, Clarifications]

## The check on return

- [ ] CHK011 Is the plan's definition testable — which classes are checked by type only and which relations lead out of the list — without naming the implementation? [Measurability, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK012 Are all three hand-off points (connections, resolve, test-bench substitute) stated as subject to the check? [Coverage, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the reference rule defined — what a relation that leads out of the list must be — with an example of the passing and the refused answer? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the exact-class comparison and the partial-answer exception consistent with the reference rule, with no case that both accepts and refuses the same answer? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK015 Does every refusal name the resource, the entry point, the path and the class, and does the spec fix the message shape? [Measurability, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK016 Are the async-iterator path, the private method, the entity-free answer and the resource without `@entities` each covered as their own case? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011, §FR-012, §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK017 Is "the check always runs, no modes" stated in a way that forbids a switch later added under the same name? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]

## Pool and assembly

- [ ] CHK018 Is exactly-one-of `pool=`/`connection_params=` stated with both refusals (both, neither) and the kind that takes neither? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK019 Is it stated that the pool is absent from the model and the graph, not merely "not a resource"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK020 Are the three assembly modes (lifespan, script, test) requirements rather than examples that could be dropped? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006, §FR-007]

## Graph, versions and documentation

- [ ] CHK021 Is protocol 2.0's shape fixed — `resource_entity` from each resource to each listed entity, no resource `domain` link, an entity `domain` link, no data source vertex or edge? [Measurability, Spec §FR-014, §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK022 Is the source of the schema and of `graph-builder` named by revision, so the graph check is reproducible? [Traceability, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK023 Does the spec state which levels raise their version and why, beyond "every changed level"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK024 Are the documentation cases enumerated — the model, the check, the pool, each refusal — with the requirement that each is executed as a script and a notebook? [Coverage, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK025 Is one changelog article required in plain language with the migration, and is it placed after the check run and the documentation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017, plan §Constitution Check]

## Ambiguities and dependencies

- [ ] CHK026 Is the dependency on gnomon#66 recorded as a precondition with its revision, and does the spec say what happens if that protocol is unavailable? [Dependency, Spec §FR-014, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK027 Are the out-of-scope items (writes not bounded by domain, Maxitor's views, one transaction across two resources) stated so they cannot be read as omissions? [Clarity, Spec §Clarifications, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK028 Does the performance criterion name its measurement (ratio on the demo's entities) rather than an adjective or a microsecond target? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK029 Is the demo's migration expressed as a rule (one resource per database) rather than a list that can fall out of date? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015, plan §Design]
- [ ] CHK030 Are the terms "reference", "partial answer" and "listed entity" used with one meaning across the spec, the plan and the research note? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, plan §Design]

## Notes

- Focus areas: removal completeness, the check on return, migration surfaces. Depth: Standard. Audience: reviewer before implementation.
- `checklists/requirements.md` is the separate spec-quality checklist maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`; the items above are a migration gate and stay unchecked until the reviewer evaluates them.
- `/speckit-implement` reads this state and does not change markers.
